clue.text: Promise to donate an arm

parts.note: to donate is to give something away
an, meaning a single one, gives the numeral word
an arm is a weapon, and a sword is an example of one

explanation.surface: Someone vows to hand over a limb, a grisly pledge indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' looks like a limb, but here it is a weapon. The pieces run on without the apostrophe, so GIVE ONE SWORD reads as the phrase meaning to pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge solemnly that you will do something is to make a firm promise.

clue.text: Complain about gruel prepared by doctor inside

indicators.note: inside says the doctor goes within the rearranged letters
gruel that has been prepared is cooked up, so its letters are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A patient moans about the porridge cooked by the physician on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' mixes up the porridge and 'inside' slots the doctor into the mix; 'about' simply links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble is to mutter discontentedly, which is to complain.

clue.text: Launch this boat when vet teed off

indicators.note: off, meaning gone wrong or out of order, tells us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Instructions to launch a boat once the vet has taken a tee shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges VETTEED. A vedette is a small naval patrol launch, and 'this boat when' just links the definition to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A vedette is a small fast naval patrol boat, a type of motor launch.

clue.text: One who gets a poor press strangely or quite fittingly

definitions.text: One who gets a poor press strangely or quite fittingly

indicators.note: strangely tells us to arrange the letters of poor press in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A tyrant gets bad reviews in the newspapers, and deservedly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges POORPRESS. The rest of the clue comments that a tyrant deserves bad coverage, so the whole clue serves as the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant who crushes people is the sort of figure the newspapers rightly condemn.

clue.text: Assume that bear has no right

indicators.note: has no says a letter is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: to bear something is to endure it

explanation.surface: Someone supposes that a bear lacks any entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning put up with. 'Assume' is used in its sense of putting on, as of a quality or garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to put on or take on a quality, just as one may assume an air.

clue.text: Man takes marijuana round for days two days

indicators.note: round says the marijuana goes around the man

parts.note: weed is slang for marijuana
Ken is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man takes cannabis about with him for a couple of days off.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'days' looks like a doubled word in the printed text and acts only as a link; 'takes ... round' puts the man inside the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturday and Sunday together make up the two-day break at the end of the working week.

clue.text: Composer finds island in Italian capital

parts.note: Ross Island lies in Antarctica's Ross Sea

indicators.note: capital means the first, upper-case letter of the word Italian

explanation.surface: A musician discovers an island lying within the chief city of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian capital' wants to be Rome; it is only the first letter I. 'finds' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian who wrote the opera The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Is one bent on breaking the law?

definitions.text: Is one bent on breaking the law?

parts.words: Is one bent on breaking the law?
parts.note: bent means both crooked and determined; someone determined to commit crime is a master criminal, and bent also suggests a curved arch

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone is set on committing crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading villain is set on breaking the law, and arches are bent in shape.

clue.text: Raise a collection of suspects perhaps

definitions.meaning: to increase a figure to the next whole number, as with a price
a police gathering-in of people suspected of a crime

explanation.surface: Police raise funds by gathering up likely culprits.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is increasing a number to the next whole figure; the other is a mass arrest of suspects.

clue.text: Welsh theatre attendant?

parts.note: a Welsh piece of kitchen furniture shares its name with a backstage helper who looks after actors' costumes

explanation.surface: A query about an usher working in a theatre in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: A Welsh dresser is a kitchen cabinet with open shelves; in the theatre a dresser helps actors with costumes.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre helper who looks after costumes is called by the same name as the Welsh sideboard.

clue.text: Go back to harbour for another drink

definitions.meaning: a ship heading home to its harbour
having a second glass of the fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Sailors head back into harbour for one more drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship sails home to harbour; a drinker goes back to the fortified wine for another glass.

clue.text: One frequenting a posh part first he goes round

indicators.note: goes round says the word he surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first says the part comes before posh, though printed after it

parts.note: a bit is a part of something
U, as in U and non-U, means upper-class or posh

explanation.surface: A regular visitor to a smart neighbourhood strolls around it first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the part ahead of posh, though printed after it, and 'goes round' wraps the pronoun around everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitue is a regular visitor to a place such as a club or bar.

clue.text: Lie gets distorted by the writer

indicators.note: distorted means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A falsehood is twisted by an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges LIEGETS; 'by' links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist is a poet who writes elegies, mournful verses for the dead.

clue.text: Steward at some more events

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A steward is present at several further occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to a run of letters inside 'more events'.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval England a reeve was an official managing an estate on a lord's behalf.

clue.text: Machine to go round with rider stumbling

parts.note: to go round is to spin

indicators.note: stumbling suggests a jumbled tumble, so the letters of rider are mixed up

explanation.surface: A machine spins about as a rider trips.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin-drier is a household appliance that whirls wet laundry to remove water.

clue.text: I am to intercede next

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
to intercede is to step in between parties, to mediate

explanation.surface: Someone announces they will step in and arbitrate after this.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate means coming straight after, with nothing between, as in the next house.

clue.text: Eddy disturbed smart mole

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Eddy upset a clever burrowing mammal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eddy' looks like a man's name; it is a swirl of water. 'disturbed' rearranges SMARTMOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, a violent swirl of water.

clue.text: In progress moving net before the bad weather

indicators.note: before places the rearranged letters ahead of the next piece
moving means shifting about, so the letters of net change places

parts.note: rain is a common kind of bad weather

explanation.surface: Fishermen shift their nets ahead of the storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns NET into ENT. 'En train' is borrowed from French and means under way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something under way, already happening, is said to be en train.

clue.text: Staff Officer hurried into the river for the singer

parts.note: SO is the military abbreviation for Staff Officer

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
hurried means ran

explanation.surface: A military officer rushes into a river to save a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' drops the verb inside the Italian river, after the officer's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano sings in the highest female or boy's voice range.

clue.text: Bird, it goes after seed

indicators.note: goes after says the word it follows the seed in the answer

parts.note: a pip is a fruit's seed

explanation.surface: A bird chases after some grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit is a small brownish songbird of open country.

clue.text: Head across the border for a religious leader

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the head lies over the border on both sides

parts.note: the pate is the top of the head
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A clergyman's chief crosses the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a leader, but it is the crown of the skull, which 'across' stretches over the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is an archbishop, the senior bishop of a church province.

clue.text: Stop couple shortly before the race

indicators.note: before places the couple ahead of the race

parts.note: PR is the short form of pair, a couple
a race is a sporting event

explanation.surface: Two people halt just before the race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it from happening.

clue.text: On returning record about model, notice the paper

indicators.note: returning means the word On is read backwards

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car; about is a loose link meaning concerning
an EP is an extended-play record
an ad is a notice advertising something

explanation.surface: Coming back, someone writes about a model and spots the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the first word round. 'about' is a loose link meaning alongside: the record sits next to the model.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a block of sheets for jotting on, a form of writing paper.

clue.text: Lived a long time and kept on about it

definitions.meaning: lingered on a subject, talking at length about it

explanation.surface: Someone has lived ages and never stops talking about it.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is resided; the other is lingered over a subject in speech or thought.

clue.text: Arrive in a vehicle whilst the road is being repaired

parts.note: a drive is a road, often a private one
a road that is up is dug up for repair works

explanation.surface: A motorist pulls in while roadworks are going on.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a road that is 'up' is closed for repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive up is to arrive somewhere by car.

clue.text: Reason one may not be able to see the wood for the trees

definitions.text: Reason one may not be able to see the wood for the trees

parts.words: Reason one may not be able to see the wood for the trees
parts.note: the idiom about missing the big picture is read literally: what hides the timber of the trunks is the foliage

explanation.surface: An explanation of why someone misses the big picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage on the branches hides the timber of the trunks behind it.

clue.text: Article by unusually mature layman

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of mature appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece placed next to a surprisingly grown-up non-professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the adjective; 'by' means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur is a non-professional, like a layman lacking specialist expertise.

clue.text: Splendid person who is hard to beat

definitions.meaning: a first-rate individual, a real gem
someone among the top performers, difficult to defeat

explanation.surface: A fine fellow who rarely loses.
explanation.definitionFit: A top individual counts among the finest, and so is very difficult to surpass.
